description: Distribution warehouse operations: receiving, putaway, picking, counting, hazardous goods and returns.

units.title: Receiving against an ASN
units.text: Inbound trucks are unloaded only when an advance shipping notice (ASN) exists in the system. A delivery without an ASN waits in the yard until purchasing creates one or rejects the load.

units.title: Advance shipping notice
units.text: An electronic message sent by the supplier before dispatch that lists the pallets, SKUs, quantities and lot numbers of a shipment. Receiving staff scan each pallet against it.

units.title: Putaway
units.text: After receipt, the warehouse management system proposes a location based on SKU velocity and pallet height. The operator scans the pallet label and then the location label; a putaway without the location scan is blocked.

units.title: Picking follows FEFO, not FIFO
units.text: For products with an expiry date, pickers take the lot that expires first, even when a newer lot arrived earlier. FIFO applies only to items without an expiry date.

units.title: Cycle counting
units.text: Fast-moving A items are counted every month, B items every quarter and C items twice a year. A location with a variance above 2% is recounted by a different operator before any adjustment is posted.

units.title: Hazardous goods segregation
units.text:
| Hazard class | Storage rule |
|---|---|
| Flammable liquids (class 3) | Fire-rated cabinet, at most 250 litres per aisle |
| Oxidisers (class 5.1) | At least 3 metres away from flammable liquids |
| Corrosives (class 8) | Bunded floor area with a spill kit |

units.title: Customer returns
units.text: Returned goods are inspected within 48 hours. Undamaged items in their original packaging go back to stock; opened or damaged items are graded B and sold through the outlet channel.

units.title: Forklift operation
units.text: Only certified operators may drive forklifts, and the certification is renewed every three years. Pedestrians may not enter an aisle while a forklift is working in it.

units.title: Dock appointments
units.text: Carriers book 60-minute unloading slots through the carrier portal. A truck that arrives more than 30 minutes late loses its slot and is rescheduled.

units.title: Warehouse KPIs
units.text:
| KPI | Target | Q3 |
|---|---|---|
| Order picking accuracy | 99.8% | 99.6% |
| Dock-to-stock time | 24 h | 31 h |
| Inventory record accuracy | 98% | 98.4% |

units.title: Cross-docking
units.text: Goods move from the inbound dock straight to an outbound dock without being put away in storage, usually within a few hours. It suits pre-allocated orders whose destination is already known at receipt.

units.title: Chilled goods never wait on the open dock
headingPath: Chilled goods never wait on the open dock
units.text: Chilled products must reach the cold room within 20 minutes of unloading. The open dock is not temperature controlled, so leaving pallets there breaks the cold chain.

units.title: Lot numbers are captured at receipt
headingPath: Lot numbers are captured at receipt
units.text: Recording the lot number of every pallet at receipt lets the warehouse locate and block all affected stock within minutes when a supplier issues a recall.

units.title: Damaged inbound pallets
units.text: When a pallet arrives damaged, the receiver photographs it, writes the damage on the delivery note before the driver signs, and moves the pallet to the quarantine lane.
